title: Graceful reconnect: stretch-window checkpointing, de-dup de-conflict, and semantic-boundary alignment for SSE
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: Some customers observe duplicated or truncated tool-call/function-call payloads after short client blips when using our SSE streaming API. Existing resume semantics rely on a single resume token and naive offset trimming which can lead to either duplicated tokens or partially applied function-call boundaries. Goal: implement a stretch-window checkpointing + de-duplication strategy that preserves semantic boundaries (complete function/tool call objects) while enabling fast reconnects and bounded memory for servers. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, tracing, and a controlled canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Reconnect flow can resume within a configurable stretch window (default: 8 chunks) without duplicating completed function-call objects
Server-side checksums allow exact duplicate detection for any chunk re-delivery within the stretch window
Partial function-call objects are never emitted to clients as completed; reconnect/resume must rehydrate partial boundary until completion or graceful abort
New metrics emitted: resume_latency_p50/p95, duplicate_chunk_rate, semantic_boundary_rewinds, resumption_failures
Backward-compatible: clients that only supply old resume token still work (legacy path) with reduced guarantees

End-to-end tests cover: normal streaming, client reconnect in middle of function call, client reconnect right after function call boundary, duplicate packet replay from proxies, and simultaneous multiplexed channels
implementation_notes: Checkpoint model: server assigns monotonically increasing ordinal chunk_id per SSE connection and computes a short checksum (CRC32c) for chunk payloads. Combine chunk_id + checksum = chunk_proof.

Stretch-window: server retains recent N chunk_proofs for each session (N default 8, configurable per-customer). On resume the client provides last_seen_chunk_id and last_seen_chunk_proof (optional). Server matches last_seen_chunk_proof within window; if match found resume point = matched chunk_id + 1; otherwise fall back to legacy resume-token negotiation.
De-dup: client and server both tolerate replay by checking chunk_proof; if an incoming chunk matches previously acknowledged chunk_proof, it is dropped before delivery to the application layer.

Semantic boundary alignment: when chunk payloads contain structured outputs (JSONL fragments or function_call frames), we enforce that only full structured messages are considered 'committed'. If resume occurs inside an uncommitted structured message, the server buffers and replays from the start of that message OR requests client to re-issue (in case of non-idempotent tool calls).

Tool/function-call safety: function_call frames include an explicit frame header with call_id and status (start/continuation/end). We will extend headers to include a 'boundary_hash' computed over the function_call canonical form to validate integrity across resumes.

Compatibility layers: implement negotiation header 'X-RI-Resume-Mode' with values 'legacy', 'stretch-v1'. Default to 'legacy' for older clients; enable 'stretch-v1' for new SDKs and the Console. Server logs will tag resume_mode for telemetry and gradual rollout.

Memory/cost: retain only last N chunk_proofs per active session; chunk payload retention is optional and gated by memory budget — prefer proof-only retention plus temporary payload cache for active reconnects. If payload unavailable and match required, trigger slow-path reconcilers: accept less-optimal fallback and mark semantic_boundary_rewinds metric.

Backpressure & failure modes: if stream backlog grows during reconnect window, the server may return 429 with suggested backoff and a diagnostic resume token. Define a hard TTL for session checkpoint state (default 2 minutes).
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Initial spike meeting with infra, runtime, and SDK. Agreed on chunk_proof approach and stretch-window heuristic. Identified compatibility header and metric list.

2026-03-11: Prototype implemented in runtime branch 'eng/ENG-214512/stretch-resume'. Prototype simulates chunk_id assignment and CRC proofs; added basic duplicate drop logic. Integration tests in runtime harness pass for single-connection cases.

2026-03-12: SDK changes scoped: JS and Python SDKs will send 'X-RI-Resume-Mode: stretch-v1' and include last_seen_chunk_proof in resume handshake. SDK PR draft created. Open question: whether mobile SDKs should default to 'legacy' due to offline constraints — flagged for PM decision.

Next: extend prototype to handle function_call frame headers and implement boundary_hash verification. Add end-to-end tests for proxy replay scenarios. Schedule design review with Security for checksum algorithm and potential side-channel concerns.
notes_and_risks: Risk: checksum leakage could allow an attacker to fingerprint outputs. Mitigation: use short non-cryptographic checksum but avoid exposing payloads in logs; security to review telemetry labels.

Risk: partial function-call replay may cause duplicate side-effects for non-idempotent tool integrations. Mitigation: require tool integrations to be idempotent or attach explicit call_id+boundary_hash; Console docs to advise partners.
Operational: need new dashboards to alert on duplicate_chunk_rate spike and resumed_sessions_without_match.
Edge-case: multiplexed streams (multiple channels on single connection) will require per-channel ordinal spaces; plan to add channel_id scoping to chunk_id namespace in next iteration.
